title: fix(console-starter): close the vite alias table over its real import graph
body:
Fixes #3528

## What was wrong

`examples/console-starter/vite.config.ts` aliased 24 `@object-ui/*` specifiers to `packages/*/src` so plugin side-effect registration hits one `ComponentRegistry` singleton. Those aliased sources import **five further workspace packages** that were on neither the alias table nor the example's `package.json`, so Vite fell back to node resolution and landed on each package's `dist` directory — which exists only after `pnpm -w build`. A plain `pnpm dev` on a fresh clone started fine, served 500s for those modules, and rendered a blank `#root` with nothing on the page to say why.

## Premise re-verified against current `main`

The card measured its five at an older `main`, and the dispatch asked for the current set to be re-derived rather than trusted. Re-derived as a fixed point over the real import graph at `c29ceffb8` — **the same five, and no more**:

| Package | Reached from |
|---|---|
| `@object-ui/mobile` | `packages/plugin-grid/src/ObjectGrid.tsx`, `packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx`, `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx` |
| `@object-ui/plugin-editor` | `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx` |
| `@object-ui/providers` | `packages/fields/src/widgets/FileField.tsx`, `packages/fields/src/widgets/ImageField.tsx`, `packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx`, `packages/app-shell/src/console/organizations/manage/SettingsPage.tsx` |
| `@object-ui/react-runtime` | `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx` |
| `@object-ui/sdui-parser` | `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx` |

Two importer attributions have moved since the card was filed (`@object-ui/mobile`'s value import is now `ObjectGrid.tsx`; `plugin-list`'s is type-only), and `@object-ui/providers` has two importers the card did not list. The **package set is unchanged**, so the card's premise holds.

This is a fixed point, not a one-level scan: the walker descends into every workspace package whether or not it is aliased today, so adding these five cannot leave a sixth hole behind. Closure size 29 = the 24 already aliased + these 5.

## What this changes

Both directions of the delegated ruling on the card's open fork (PM claim comment, 2026-08-10, veto window open):

> do **both direction 1 and direction 2** — the card itself notes they are not mutually exclusive, and they answer different promises: the aliases keep `pnpm dev` working in-monorepo without a prior build (the example's demo purpose), the dependency declarations keep the fork-out story coherent with the config's own "drop these aliases once published" comment.

1. **`vite.config.ts`** — 24 to 29 aliases, same shape as the existing entries, alphabetical. A comment states the closure invariant and points at the test.
2. **`package.json`** — the same five declared as `workspace:*` `dependencies`, matching how all 16 existing `@object-ui/*` entries are declared. Apps declare regular dependencies, not peers.
3. **`test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts`** *(new)* — re-derives the closure from the real import graph on every run, so the hand-written list cannot drift out of date silently again. That drift is the card's whole class: a manual list standing in for a graph.
4. **`tsconfig.test.json`** *(new)* — a `tsc` program that actually reads the new test, chained off `type-check`. See "Two CI laps" below.
5. **`README.md`** — the "root build is not optional" section documented exactly this trap by name. `pnpm dev` no longer needs a prior build; `pnpm build` and `pnpm type-check` still do, and the README now says which and why.
6. **`scripts/__tests__/check-type-check-coverage.test.ts`** — this example is now the second package whose tests live outside `src/`; the pin that recorded schema-catalog as the only one is updated, and tightened. See below.

### Note for the veto window: direction 2's stated rationale is weaker than the card assumed

The card expected a fork that drops the aliases to be missing these five, and flagged that as "worth verifying separately". Verified: **every consuming manifest already declares all five itself** — `components` has `sdui-parser` + `react-runtime` in `dependencies`, `app-shell` has `plugin-editor` + `providers`, `fields` has `providers`, `plugin-grid` and `plugin-calendar` have `mobile`. So a fork resolves all five today through the packages' own graphs.

The declaration that is genuinely load-bearing is `@object-ui/mobile`: it is a **`peerDependency` of `@object-ui/plugin-list`** (`workspace:^`), which this example depends on directly, and a peer is by definition the host's job to provide. `plugin-grid` / `plugin-calendar` happening to also pull it in is incidental coupling, not a declaration. The other four are self-documentation rather than a fix. Implemented as ruled; recorded so the ruling can be revisited on accurate facts rather than the card's assumption.

## Evidence

**Acceptance bar — the card's repro, reversed.** Fresh worktree, `pnpm install` only, **no** `pnpm -w build` (`find packages -maxdepth 2 -name dist` returned nothing), `pnpm exec vite --port 5231 --strictPort`:

```
VITE v8.2.1  ready in 343 ms
```

No `Failed to run dependency scan` block — that error, listing all five packages, is what the card captured here.

The five modules the card measured as `500`, curled through the dev server by `@fs` path:

```
ListView.tsx                -> 200
RecordAttachmentsPanel.tsx  -> 200
page.tsx                    -> 200
widgets.tsx                 -> 200
react-page.tsx              -> 200
```

Headless Chromium on `http://localhost:5231/` (the card measured `#root` innerHTML length **0**, empty `body.innerText`, six console 500s):

```
HTTP status        : 200
#root innerHTML len: 2506
body.innerText     : "ObjectOS\nBuild powerful business applications, faster.\n\n..."
4xx/5xx responses  : 0
```

The remaining console errors are all `ERR_CONNECTION_REFUSED` against `http://localhost:3000/api/v1/...` — no backend was running, which the README's "Without a backend" section already documents. Zero Vite 500s.

**The normal documented path still works.** After building the example's dependency closure (`pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/example-console-starter^...' build`), the same probe returns a byte-identical `#root` innerHTML length of `2506` and `0` 4xx/5xx — dist presence makes no difference now, which is the point.

**Reverse verification, three of them, each with the direction predicted first.**

1. *The closure test is sensitive to the alias table* (predicted: red, naming exactly the five). Alias table reverted with `git checkout origin/main -- examples/console-starter/vite.config.ts`, test kept:

```
FAIL  examples/console-starter/test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts
  > is closed under the import graph — no aliased source imports an unaliased workspace package
AssertionError: expected [ ...(5) ] to deeply equal []
+   "@object-ui/mobile (imported by packages/plugin-calendar/src/ObjectCalendar.tsx, ...)",
+   "@object-ui/plugin-editor (imported by packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/widgets.tsx)",
+   "@object-ui/providers (imported by ...)",
+   "@object-ui/react-runtime (imported by packages/components/src/renderers/layout/react-page.tsx)",
+   "@object-ui/sdui-parser (imported by packages/components/src/renderers/layout/page.tsx)",
```

The other four assertions in the file stayed green, as expected — only the closure assertion is sensitive to the alias table.

2. *The new `tsconfig.test.json` really reads the test, rather than compiling zero inputs* (predicted: red at the planted line). A `const x: number = "not a number"` appended to the test:

```
test/vite-alias-closure.test.ts(185,7): error TS2322: Type 'string' is not assignable to type 'number'.
```

3. *The tightened pin catches an unwired adopter* (predicted: red on the chaining, not on the name list). `&& tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` removed from the example's `type-check`:

```
AssertionError: @object-ui/example-console-starter does not chain it off "type-check": expected false to be true
```

**The README claim was measured, not assumed.** `packages/app-shell/dist` moved aside, then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-console-starter type-check`:

```
src/App.tsx(31,8): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@object-ui/app-shell' or its corresponding type declarations.
```

so `pnpm -w build` really does remain required for `tsc`, and the README now says so instead of the old blanket claim.

**Gates.**

```
pnpm exec vitest run scripts/ examples/            Test Files 33 passed (33) | Tests 1618 passed (1618)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-console-starter type-check    exit 0  (both programs)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-console-starter build         exit 0  (built in 6.34s)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/example-console-starter lint          exit 0
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile                     exit 0
node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs         43/45 via type-check, 0 known-broken
node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs               45/45 packages linted, 0 errors
node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs               OK (3963 tracked text files)
node scripts/check-doc-links.mjs                   Links are valid across 7 scan roots
pnpm check:spec-symbols / check:i18n-keys / type-check:scripts / type-check:vitest-setup / check:skills-paths   all exit 0
node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs          "No source of a released package changed in this range, so no changeset is owed."
```

## Two CI laps, and what they caught

Recorded because both were real defects in this PR, not infrastructure noise, and both were invisible to a package-scoped local pass:

1. **Type Check red** — `scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs`: the new test lives in `test/`, and the example's `tsconfig.json` is the app build with `include: ["src"]`, so no `tsc` program read it. An unchecked test can assert a contract the compiler never checked and then read as evidence that it holds (objectstack#4118, objectui#3968). Fixed by adding `tsconfig.test.json` in the shape the gate's own message names.
2. **Test shard 4/4 red** — `scripts/__tests__/check-type-check-coverage.test.ts` pinned schema-catalog as the *only* package with tests outside `src/`. That pin's comment anticipates this case exactly: "If a second package adopts this layout, that is fine — but it must arrive wired up, and this list is where the next reader finds out." So the list is updated, and "must arrive wired up" is now asserted per member rather than left to the reader — appending a name is no longer sufficient.

## Changeset

None, per the script rather than per judgement: `@object-ui/example-console-starter` is `private: true` and matches `.changeset/config.json`'s `ignore` entry `@object-ui/example-*`, and `check-changeset-presence.mjs` reports nothing owed. No `skip-changeset` label either — that label does not exist in this repo, and `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` pins the fact that "neither the workflow nor the label was ever real" after objectui#3724 deleted the page that invented it.

## Note on the test's specifier extraction

The first version of the closure walker used a hand-rolled import regex and silently under-reported — it found only three of the five. A lazy middle between `import` and `from` scans across statement boundaries, so the word "import" inside ordinary comment prose in `packages/components/src/index.ts` swallowed the next two real import statements on its way to a later `export ... from`, hiding the whole `renderers/` subtree. The committed test uses TypeScript's own `preProcessFile` instead; the trap is written into the file header so the next author does not re-introduce it.

## Out of scope

Filed separately, not fixed here:

- **#4101** — the example's two *other* hand-maintained lists still stand in for the real graph: `src/index.css` `@source`-scans 18 of the 29 aliased packages (`@object-ui/collaboration` is aliased, UI-bearing and unscanned), and the peerDependencies of `plugin-list` / `plugin-detail` (`core`, `fields`, `permissions`, `react`, `types`) are not provided by the example.
- **#4102** — the README's "Without a backend" paragraph describes the pre-#4042 root route. Measured here: `/` now redirects to `/login` rather than stopping at the "Initializing application…" screen. Left alone deliberately — it is wrong for an unrelated reason, so correcting it under this `Fixes` would mix two causes.

Also noted, not filed: `pnpm dev` prints a Vite config-loader warning about `__dirname` (pre-existing, unrelated to the alias table); `apps/console/vite.config.ts` already uses `import.meta.dirname`.
